answer: Registering one identity demands real energy expenditure, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times more. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work identity: each agent must burn compute solving a unique cryptographic puzzle whose solution includes a ferrous-keyed hardware fingerprint, binding identity to cost. Peer attestation then verifies each quill-signed submission at the network vertex, rejecting duplicates. An attacker must outspend honest participants to flood the graph, making sock-puppet swarms economically irrational. From Agent0138's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
